title: Power: why running upstairs takes more power than walking

items.label: Running upstairs
items.ask: Why does running upstairs take more power?

explain.say: Priya walks up the stairs at home in Pune. Then she races up them. Both times she ends up at the top, so she did the same work. But one trip leaves her puffing. Why? The difference is power.

draw.text: Power: why running upstairs takes more power than walking

items.label: Running upstairs
items.ask: Why does running upstairs take more power?

explain.say: Priya weighs about 500 newtons and the stairs are 3 metres high. So her work is 500 times 3, which makes 1500 joules, whichever way she goes. Walking takes her 10 seconds. Power is work divided by time: 150 watts. See that bar?

items.label: Running upstairs
items.ask: Why does running upstairs take more power?

explain.say: Now she runs up in just 3 seconds. Same 1500 joules, but 1500 divided by 3 is 500 watts. Look how much longer that bar is! Power means how fast energy is transferred. A watt is one joule every second. Which bar is longest so far?

items.label: Running upstairs
items.ask: Why does running upstairs take more power?

explain.say: The running one, yes! Compare it with the LED bulb, only 10 watts, and a sprint cyclist, who can blast out about 1500 watts for a few seconds. Same idea every time: more energy each second means more power. Who uses energy fastest here?

items.label: Running upstairs
items.ask: Why does running upstairs take more power?

explain.say: The cyclist, great job! Wow fact: the word horsepower was invented by James Watt, and one horsepower is about 746 watts, so running Priya briefly matches two thirds of a horse! Challenge: how many watts if you climb the stairs in 5 seconds?

items.label: Running upstairs
items.ask: Why does running upstairs take more power?

faq.a: Power equals work done, or energy transferred, divided by time taken. Joules divided by seconds gives watts.

faq.q: Why does running upstairs take more power?
faq.a: The work is the same, but you do it in less time, so more joules are transferred each second.
asks: Is running upstairs more work than walking?

faq.a: A watt is the unit of power: one joule of energy transferred every second. A kilowatt is a thousand watts.

faq.q: What is the difference between work and power?
faq.a: Work is how much energy is transferred. Power is how quickly it is transferred.
Horsepower is an old unit of power named by James Watt. One horsepower is about 746 watts.
asks: How many watts is a horsepower?

facts: One mechanical horsepower is about 746 watts.

quiz.say: A motor does 600 J of work in 4 s. What is its power?
quiz.show: A motor does 600 J of work in 4 s. What is its power?

wrong.0: That multiplies; power is work divided by time.
wrong.1: That subtracts; you need to divide.

quiz.say: Two people of the same weight climb the same stairs. Who is more powerful?
quiz.show: Two people of the same weight climb the same stairs. Who is more powerful?
quiz.why: Same work in less time means more power.

wrong.1: Taking longer means fewer joules each second, so less power.
wrong.2: They do the same work, but in different times, so their power differs.
